Threshold Settings

                ℹ️
                Settings & Severity Guide (What do these mean?)
                ▾
              
              

                

                  
Severity Levels Explained

                  
    
                    
  • LOW Minor Anomaly: Brief eye wander or small posture adjustment. Logged for informational review; does not interrupt or penalize the student.
    • 
                    
  • MEDIUM Suspicious Action: Prolonged gaze away from screen or head turned toward notes/second display. Flags warning for proctor review.
    • 
                    
  • HIGH Probable Misconduct: Candidate absent from chair or unauthorized device (smartphone) visible. Triggers immediate proctor alert.
    • 
                    
  • CRITICAL Severe Violation: Another person assisting in frame, impersonation/proxy test-taker, or camera feed covered. Grounds for exam pause or disqualification.
    • 
                  

                

                

                  
Detection Rules & Thresholds

                  
Gaze Off Screen: Flags when eyes look left/right or up/down past display boundaries. Hold time absorbs natural eye blinking.

                  
Head Turned Away: Flags when head orientation exceeds yaw (left/right) or pitch (up/down) limits.

                  
No Face / Multi Face: Tracks candidate presence. Hold timer ensures someone briefly bending down doesn't trigger false alarms.

                  
Identity Match: Cosine similarity against enrolled face. Scores below threshold indicate a different person.

                  
Prohibited Objects: Detects smartphones and devices using accumulated evidence to prevent false alarms from fleeting shadows.

                  
Signal Lost: Alerts if camera is covered or video feed stops. A covered lens is never reported as 'all clear'.
